requirement:
The requirements index MUST link to its execution-coverage subchapter under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index`.
rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.test-coverage.index.navigation`.

**Obligation.** The requirements index must link to its execution-coverage subchapter.

**Test.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` carries the `{test}` reference. It builds a requirements-index chapter at `reports.md` and runs the production `populate_in`. It then asserts that the index chapter's content contains `[Coverage gaps](reports/coverage.html)`. That checks the link text and the href, which is relative to the index path. It also asserts that the generated `coverage.md` chapter is the index's first sub-item and sits at `reports/coverage.md`. The test runs twice, once with a numbered index and once with an unnumbered one. The link is asserted in both runs.

**Implementation.** `populate_in` appends the link to the matching chapter's content with `chapter_href(parent, &index_path, None)`. It returns an error if the index chapter is missing. The assertion would catch a missing link, a wrong href or wrong link text.

**Scope.** Whether the index is explicitly placed or automatically generated is part of the cited `requirements.test-coverage.index`. Other tests cover that requirement, so I did not reassess it here. The link is added in `populate_in`, which is the same path the test exercises.

I found no gaps and no acknowledgments.
